## REASONING

The user's actual question — "how much will water levels recover over a decade if agricultural pumping is cut 30%" — is a **transient groundwater management** problem. That mechanism (pumping stress on an aquifer, and its relaxation) is fundamentally outside what the primary model (ELM, a 1-D land-surface column) represents. ELM has no pumping sink, no lateral groundwater flow, and no regional water-table solver. It produces recharge/drainage (QDRAI) at the bottom of its soil column, but it cannot translate a change in pumping into a water-table trajectory.

The only model in the stack that touches subsurface flow is PFLOTRAN, and it is documented as **steady-state groundwater only** — it cannot produce a decadal transient recovery curve, and the ELM→PFLOTRAN coupler is **not implemented**. On top of the model gaps, the single most important input — **pumping records** — is explicitly listed as missing. Without baseline pumping, a "30% reduction" scenario has no quantitative anchor.

So the core question is **infeasible** as posed. I will not dress this up as a coupling design that we can execute; I'll flag it honestly and list the backlog.

What the stack *can* contribute is the **recharge boundary condition** side of the problem: ELM single-column runs across the basin's soil/management heterogeneity can estimate spatially-variable recharge (QDRAI) under 1980–2018 forcing, and water-table depth from those columns can be sanity-checked against USGS well observations. This is a genuine, useful sub-component — it is exactly the input a future coupled model would need — but it does NOT answer the pumping-recovery question. I therefore keep the design as an ELM recharge-characterization + well-validation campaign, stratified by soil and land management (the only listed candidate driver), and I record everything the real question needs in requires_capabilities.

Elevation range is narrow (260–420 m) and forcing is uniform, so elevation cannot be isolated as a climate driver; I use it only lightly as a landscape-position proxy for recharge/discharge zones.
